statements.claim: An asura (Vrikasura) had chased a god (Shiva) out of the heavens, and stood at the gates of Vaikuntha while the god he hunted crouched within.
statements.evidence: SB 10.88.23-25 (asura pursued the terrified Shiva, who fled trembling and took refuge in Vaikuntha, where Narayana abides); DKS_0535 pack excerpt: Shiva 'flees to the ends of the earth and heavens and finally takes refuge in Vaikuntha.'

statements.claim: The god hid 'waiting for the end his own compassion had made possible' (i.e., Shiva's boon to Vrikasura caused his own peril).
statements.evidence: Reflective framing of the boon's consequences (SB 10.88.18-22), not a separately sourceable event.

statements.claim: Vrikasura, son of Shakuni, had tormented himself with penance.
statements.evidence: SB 10.88.13 & 16: 'vṛko nāmāsuraḥ putraḥ śakuneḥ' (the asura Vrikasura, son of Shakuni); 'upādhāvat sva-gātrataḥ' (tormented his own body). Verses 12-27 are quoted in this episode's preceding story pack (DKS_0535).

statements.claim: The penance lasted seven days and nights, after which Shiva appeared.
statements.evidence: SB 10.88.17: penance until 'saptame 'hani' (the seventh day), when Shiva (mahā-kāruṇiko dhūrjaṭiḥ, v.18) appeared; DKS_0535 pack excerpt: 'performs terrible penance and wins from the compassionate Shiva the boon.'

statements.claim: Shiva offered Vrikasura any gift, and the asura chose that whoever's head he touched would die.
statements.evidence: SB 10.88.19-20 ('vitarāmi te varam' / the sinful one chose the fear-inspiring boon); DKS_0535 index summary states the boon verbatim.

statements.claim: Vrikasura doubted the boon and decided to test it on the head of Shiva himself, who fled terrified across earth and heavens.
statements.evidence: SB 10.88.22-23: 'sa tad-vara-parīkṣārthaṃ śambhor mūrdhni kilāsuraḥ' (to test the boon, on Shambhu's head); 'tenopasṛṣṭaḥ santrastaḥ parādhāvan sa-vepathuḥ.'

statements.claim: The gods looked on helpless, unable to think of any remedy.
statements.evidence: SB 10.88.24: 'ajānantaḥ prati-vidhiṃ tūṣṇīm āsan sureśvarāḥ' (the lords of the gods sat silent, knowing no countermeasure).

statements.claim: Shiva stumbled into Vaikuntha, the abode of Vishnu, 'who never turns away anyone who comes pursued.'
statements.evidence: SB 10.88.25: refuge in Vaikuntha 'yatra nārāyaṇaḥ sākṣān nyāsināṃ paramo gatiḥ'; the never-turning-away gloss is the pack's devotional reading of Vishnu as supreme refuge.

statements.claim: A young brahmachari came out to meet Vrikasura, radiant as a low fire, carrying the staff and deerskin of a wandering student, with a mild, open face.
statements.evidence: SB 10.88.26-27: Vishnu 'mekhalājina-daṇḍākṣais tejasāgnir iva jvalan' (with girdle, deerskin, staff and beads, blazing like fire); pack excerpt: 'taking the form of a radiant young brahmachari.'

statements.claim: The brahmachari greeted Vrikasura and asked where a victor like him was rushing, and Vrikasura told him everything: the penance, the boon, and his plan to test it on Shiva's own head.
statements.evidence: Dialogue frame consistent with Vishnu's feigned-conversation (10.88.29-33, addressing him as 'dānavendra'); exact greeting/recital details are connective dramatization.

statements.claim: The brahmachari feigned disbelief in the boon, saying such power over life itself could not have been given to an asura — 'you have been deceived, or you deceive yourself.'
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'feigning disbelief in Shiva's boon'; SB 10.88.32-33: 'yadi vas tatra viśrambho ... jagad-gurau / yady asatyaṃ vacaḥ śambhoḥ' (doubting whether the boon of the world-teacher could be true).

statements.claim: The brahmachari suggested Vrikasura prove the boon by placing his hand on his own head, and the bewildered asura did so.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: Vishnu 'tells him to test it by placing his hand on his own head. The bewildered asura does so'; SB 10.88.34-35.

statements.claim: Vrikasura's skull split and he fell dead in an instant, slain by the very power he meant to use on a god.
statements.evidence: SB 10.88.35: 'athāpatad bhinna-śirāḥ vrajāhata iva kṣaṇāt' (he fell, head split, as if struck by a thunderbolt in a moment); pack excerpt: 'instantly splits his own skull and dies.'

statements.claim: The gods who had watched helplessly released showers of flowers when Vrikasura was killed.
statements.evidence: SB 10.88.36: 'mumucuḥ puṣpa-varṣāṇi hate pāpe vṛkāsure' (they released showers of flowers when the sinful Vrikasura was slain).

statements.claim: Shiva, freed, stepped out from hiding and stood before Vishnu, praising him as the deliverer of the great from those who offend them; he declared that no creature that wronged the great has ever survived, and that Vrikasura was destroyed by his own gift, not by Vishnu.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'the freed Shiva praises Vishnu, the deliverer of those who offend the great'; SB 10.88.37-38 ('muktaṃ giriśam ... puruṣottamaḥ', 'hataḥ ko nu mahatsv īśa jantur vai kṛta-kilbiṣaḥ'). The bare Sanskrit of v.37 grammatically reads 'Purushottama addressed the freed Girisha,' but the pack's rendered excerpt — the intended reading — assigns the praise to Shiva, and the story follows it.

statements.claim: 'Shiva rested again in Vaikuntha before returning to his own mountain, and the asura's body lay where it had fallen, a lesson in the shape of a corpse: a boon is only as safe as the hand that holds it.'
statements.evidence: Closural aftermath and moralizing atmosphere; no sourceable event asserted beyond the pack (Shiva's own mountain = generic Kailasa allusion).

notes: No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED claims. Recapitulatory backstory (Shakuni parentage, seven-day penance, chase) is grounded in SB 10.88.13/16-25, quoted across the episode's two packs (DKS_0535 covers 10.88.12-27, DKS_0536 covers 28-38 of the same chapter); cited accordingly. vv. 37-38 raw grammar is ambiguous as to speaker but the pack's excerpt is the intended reading and the story matches it.
